The '''1969–70 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|67th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|38th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The club finished in a disappointing sixth place marking the end of "Ye-yé" era, six points below of Champion [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Diario Marca|title=La flor del Real Madrid Yé-yé|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> For second consecutive year, in [[1969–70 European Cup|European Cup]] the team was early eliminated in Eightfinals by underdog Belgian side [[Standard Liège]] losing the two legs of the series in two weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.walfoot.be/news/2020-03-24/-il-fut-un-temps-le-standard-battait-le-real-madrid-deux-fois-en-deux-semaines|title=Il Fut un Temps, Le Standard battait Le Real Madrid deux fois en deux semaines|publisher=walfoot.be|language=French}}</ref>

During June in [[1970 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]] the club advanced stages, in Quarterfinals defeated [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]] 2–0 in Madrid and a controversial draw 1–1 in the second leg was suspended by referee Guruceta five minutes before the ending due to fans rioting on the field.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20131024/fc-barcelona/clasicos-barca-madrid-el-escandalo-guruceta_54390776428.html |title= The Guruceta Scandal |work=Mundo Deportivo|author=Begoña Villarrubia|language=Spanish}}</ref> Eventually the squad won the Final against [[Valencia CF]] at [[Camp Nou|Estadio del CF Barcelona]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/copa70.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091003005534/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/copa70.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=3 October 2009 |title=Copa del Rey 1970|publisher=linguasport.com}}</ref> with the national cup title serving as a consolation in the first campaign since 1952–53 where the club did not clinch a League title, neither a European Cup. Also, [[Amancio Amaro|Amancio]] won the [[Pichichi Trophy]] scoring 16 goals tied along [[José Eulogio Gárate]] and [[Luis Aragonés]].
